claim_accuracy_assessment.$725M_2025: CONFIRMED — Verisk CargoNet primary press release, Jan 22 2026. Scope: US + Canada. Category: cargo theft (physical + scheme/fraud). Note: this is CargoNet-tracked theft, not a comprehensive 'all freight fraud' figure.
claim_accuracy_assessment.$454.9M_2024: CONFIRMED — CargoNet 2024 Annual Report PDF, exact figure $454,914,764. Scope: US + Canada.
claim_accuracy_assessment.$35B_NICB_unreported: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED with attribution caveat — NICB does use this figure; however, original source is Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), not an NICB-authored study. The 'including unreported' framing is common in industry descriptions of this figure but lacks a traceable primary NICB report citation. The figure may also pre-date 2024-2025 and not be current.

terminology_note: The claim uses 'freight fraud' but Verisk CargoNet tracks 'supply chain crime' which includes cargo theft, fictitious pickup/identity schemes, and strategic theft. The CargoNet figures are the most authoritative available for North America but do not equal a comprehensive 'freight fraud' total (e.g., double brokering, payment fraud are not included). The claim should clarify it refers to cargo theft losses, not all freight fraud.
revised_claim_text: North American cargo theft losses reached an estimated ~$725 million in 2025 (up ~60% from $454.9M in 2024), per Verisk CargoNet's annual analysis covering the United States and Canada (Verisk, January 2026). Total annual US cargo theft losses including unreported incidents are estimated at up to $35 billion by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI/DHS), a figure also cited by NICB. Note: the $725M and $454.9M figures cover tracked incidents only; the $35B estimate includes significant unreported crime.
